text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Sharp oil price rise will lift inflation by at least 0.3
pct to 2.55 pct in 1997, says Central Planning Bureau (CPB). (1)
- MPs displeased with Smit Internationale insider trading
probe. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange to require members to pay margins
for settlement of stock transactions. (p1)
- Insurance body GAK to publicly sell 37 offices worth Dfl
- Copier maker Oce van der Grinten takes over Swiss rival
Messerli. (p3)
- Steel maker Hoogovens and German trader Kloeckner reach
agreement on reshuffling joint activities. (p3)
- Unilever seeks partner for German unit Nordsee. (p5)
- Amsterdam Options Traders (AOT) books 30 pct higher Q3
net at Dfl 9.3 mln. (p13)
VOLKSKRANT
- New Dutch passport easy to falsify despite precautions.
- Economic Affairs minister Hans Wijers appoints Floris
Maljers, who also conducted talks with Germany's DASA, to
negotiate with Samsung on Fokker takeover. (p2)
- Copier maker Oce van der Grinten books nearly 40 million
guilders higher third quarter net. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Economic Affairs minister retains gas exploration in
Waddenzee. (p1)
- Insurer Achmea reports 15 million guilder embezzlement by
former director of Avero unit. (p3)
- Philips Electronics seeks buyers for medical systems plant
in Best. (p41)
- Builder Heymans to sell subsidiary De Oude IJssel. (p41)
TROUW
- Employers association VNO-NCW says cabinet and parliament
interfere too much with matters better left to social partners.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Banks Credit Lyonnais and ING lose 40 milion guilders on
modern sludge processing plant in Hengelo. (p3)
- Papermaker KNP BT unit BT Office Products' third quarter
results disappointing. (p11)
